baseline_models.focus_anchor: The doubled enter/exit pair in لن ندخلها حتى يخرجوا منها ... فإن يخرجوا منها فإنا داخلون.
baseline_models.mechanism: The speakers model the land as an exclusive container: the resident group must first cross outward before the speakers will cross inward. Entry is not coordinated with struggle or coexistence but unlocked by prior vacancy.

activation_trace.role: Literal movement into an interior supplies the speakers' deferred action and the inward pole of an exclusive-occupancy mechanism.
Literal emergence from a place is assigned to the occupants as the prerequisite that unlocks the speakers' entry.
Coercion and domination explain why the occupants are imagined as controlling whether the speakers can move.

changed_reading.before: They simply refuse because powerful people inhabit the land.
changed_reading.after: They impose a zero-sum occupancy rule in which their own entry is defined as the consequence of the other group's prior exit.

baseline_models.focus_anchor: قالوا followed by the tightly formulated حتى and فإن ... فإن condition.
baseline_models.mechanism: The utterance behaves like a counterproposal: the speakers do not issue an unqualified no, but rewrite action as a bargain whose initiating movement belongs entirely to the occupants. Their agency begins only after danger has removed itself.

activation_trace.role: Negotiation over an affair makes the opening speech a counterproposal, while the until/if clauses state its terms.
Entry supplies the action the speakers conditionally retain for themselves.
Exit supplies the prior action assigned to the other group, shifting initiative away from the speakers.

changed_reading.before: The statement is a spontaneous refusal.
changed_reading.after: The statement is a negotiated countercondition that delegates all risk-bearing movement to the feared occupants.

baseline_models.focus_anchor: The paired collective expressions قوما جبارين and repeated إنا.
baseline_models.mechanism: A plural speaker-group faces an occupant-group represented as coercive in its corporate identity. Naming a whole qawm rather than discrete fighters makes domination appear environmental and total, so the speakers treat their own collective agency as already cancelled.

activation_trace.role: A human collective makes the obstacle corporate rather than individual and mirrors the speakers' plural self-positioning.
The coercive branch turns the collective description into an anticipated power to compel and overrule.

changed_reading.before: The verse reports a neutral estimate of strong residents.
changed_reading.after: The speakers construct the residents as a coercive corporate environment whose mere presence pre-cancels the speakers' capacity to act.

context_deltas.mechanism: The wider packet frames commitment as a binding that must be completed, records a prior formula of hearing and obeying, and later names the undoing of such a bond. Against that sequence, the focus utterance reads as a replacement formula: obedience is displaced by a self-authored condition that postpones action until safety is supplied by others.

activation_trace.role: Completion without deficiency frames the opening demand that commitments be carried through.
Binding and ratifying an obligation gives the packet's opening frame a contractual mechanism.
A confirmed covenant supplies the prior bond behind the reported compliance formula.
Hearing as understanding and compliance makes the earlier hearing more than sound reception.
Submission and obedience supply the pledged action that the focus condition suspends.
Undoing what was bound provides the packet's explicit failure pattern for a replacement condition.
Negotiating an affair lets the focus speech function as a newly proposed set of terms.

structural_cues: 5:1 opens with fulfillment of bindings; 5:7 records a hearing-and-obedience formula; 5:13 names covenant-breaking before the focus refusal.
The focus syntax replaces immediate performance with لن ... حتى and a repeated if/then condition.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies fulfillment, binding, prior compliance, breach vocabulary, and the focus countercondition; I infer that the later speech functions as a counter-covenant. A live alternative is that it claims only a tactical exception rather than repudiating the earlier bond.

changed_reading.before: The speakers negotiate a situational safety condition.
changed_reading.after: Their condition becomes a counter-formula that replaces pledged compliance with an obligation imposed on circumstances and opponents.

context_deltas.mechanism: Immediately before the focus, entry is an imperative toward a purified place whose allocation is established, while backward movement is prohibited. The focus transfers the first movement to the occupants and waits outside; the tactical delay therefore performs the very reversal of trajectory against which the preceding ayah warns.

activation_trace.role: Literal entry is issued as the forward action, supplying the trajectory that the focus refuses to initiate.
A purified place marks the intended interior as positively designated rather than merely dangerous territory.
An established judgment or allotment gives the entry trajectory normative force.
Return toward a prior position supplies the prohibited reverse direction.
Turning the back makes non-entry an embodied withdrawal rather than neutral waiting.
The same inward movement is retained only as a deferred consequence.
Outward movement is reassigned to the occupants, reversing who must activate the trajectory.

structural_cues: 5:21's imperative ادخلوا is answered immediately by 5:22's لن ندخلها.
The warning against turning on backs precedes the focus ayah's stationary until/if chain.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies a commanded forward entry, established destination, warning against reversal, and the focus delay; I infer that waiting outside is functionally a backward turn because it rejects the assigned first motion. The alternative is a temporary pause still oriented toward eventual entry.

changed_reading.before: They postpone entry until the threat disappears.
changed_reading.after: The postponement itself reverses a prescribed trajectory: a binding forward motion is replaced by waiting for the destination to empty itself.

context_deltas.mechanism: The nearby counter-voice supplies one sequence: cross the entrance, then dominance follows, with reliance and trust supporting the crossing. The focus supplies the inverse sequence: obtain the practical result of dominance, the occupants' departure, and only then cross. The speakers turn an expected consequence of action into its prerequisite.

activation_trace.role: Repeated literal entry places threshold-crossing before the promised outcome in the counter-voice's sequence.
The entrance localizes a concrete first step rather than requiring the whole territory to be vacant.
Prevailing force is positioned as the result that follows entry, not a pre-entry condition.
Reliance supplies the posture that permits action before control of the outcome.
Settled trust supplies the inner security paired with crossing an externally insecure threshold.
The occupants' departure substitutes for the dominance that the adjacent sequence places after entry.
Entry is delayed until its proposed consequence has effectively been secured in advance.

structural_cues: 5:23 orders entrance, completed entry, and dominance; 5:22 orders non-entry, occupant exit, and only then entry.
The two passages use closely matched conditional sequencing but assign opposite directions to the causal arrow.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies the two ordered movement sequences; I infer that occupant departure is the speakers' proxy for victory and thus that they demand the outcome before the act. A live alternative is that 5:23 offers assurance rather than a causal prediction.

changed_reading.before: The speakers prudently wait for an opening.
changed_reading.after: They invert the gate-first mechanism and demand victory's practical result before taking the first threshold-crossing action.

context_deltas.mechanism: The adjacent counter-voice places fear, reliance, and trust in the same acting subjects. That coexistence makes the focus adjective less like detached intelligence and more like fear objectified as a property of the residents: anticipated coercion is projected outward until it appears to dictate the only possible plan.

activation_trace.role: Expectation of harm supplies fear without making fear identical to paralysis.
Reliance gives fear an action-compatible counterposture.
Inner security distinguishes trust from the external conditions the focus speakers demand.
Coercive domination is the outward description into which the speakers' anticipated harm is condensed.

structural_cues: The two men of 5:23 are associated with fear yet still urge entry.
The same ayah couples their proposal with reliance and faith, while 5:22 makes external vacancy the condition of action.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies fear wording, action, reliance, trust, and the focus's coercive label; I infer that the label can be affectively saturated rather than purely descriptive. The object or construal of يخافون remains live, so the counter-voice does not prove that both groups fear the same thing.

changed_reading.before: جبارين is a neutral description of the occupants' power.
changed_reading.after: جبارين can also be heard as fear made objective: an anticipated coercion projected onto the residents until their presence seems to eliminate agency.

context_deltas.mechanism: The focus still presents a formally open condition: entry remains possible if the occupants leave. The next speech repeats non-entry but expands it into indefinite duration, sends movement and combat to others, and fixes the speakers in non-action. Context reveals the focus condition as the first stage of a self-exempting stance rather than a live plan for entry.

activation_trace.role: Repeated non-entry carries the focus condition into the next, harder formulation.
Unbounded duration removes the residual openness of the focus ayah's if-clause.
Stillness joined to continuation makes the occupants' presence a standing excuse.
Going forward is reassigned to Moses and his Lord, externalizing the movement the speakers refuse.
Mutual combat is outsourced together with movement, leaving the speakers only the benefit of any resulting vacancy.
Abstention from action turns the focus's deferred entry into an explicit identity of sitting out.
The demanded departure remains the benefit the speakers await while assigning its production elsewhere.

structural_cues: 5:24 repeats لن ندخلها but replaces the focus's until/if opening with أبدا ما داموا فيها.
Second-person going and fighting are opposed to first-person remaining here and sitting.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies the repeated refusal, duration terms, outsourced combat, and sitting; I infer that 5:24 exposes the operational tendency already present in 5:22. A live alternative is that the focus condition was initially sincere and only hardened after the counter-voice intervened.

changed_reading.before: The focus leaves a genuine future route to entry.
changed_reading.after: Its condition is the soft form of a stance that hardens into indefinite non-action while assigning every costly step to others.

context_deltas.mechanism: The focus assigns outward movement to the threatening qawm and reserves inward movement for the speakers. Afterward, qawm is attached to the speakers, separation is requested, the f-s-q branch supplies an image of something emerging from its covering, and the land is denied to them. The desired exit rebounds from the occupants onto the refusing group in social, moral, and spatial forms.

activation_trace.role: The focus assigns literal outward movement to the resident group and makes it the desired condition.
The initial collective label identifies the threatening residents as the group whose removal matters.
Distinguishing and separating two sides redirects the boundary from resident versus entrant to leader versus refusing group.
The collective label migrates from the external obstacle to the speakers as the group now under judgment.
The material image of emerging from a covering activates an exploratory moral echo of the exit the speakers demanded from others.
Prohibition turns failed entry into imposed exclusion from the desired interior.
Repetition of the exit-from-covering image sustains the rebound while the group remains outside.

structural_cues: 5:25 repeats القوم but attaches it to the refusing side and requests a division between the two parties.
5:26 makes the land forbidden and uses the branchless cue يتيهون في الأرض, turning purposeful entry into motion without arrival.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies the repeated group label, separation, prohibition, wandering, and the f-s-q branch image; I infer a deliberate-looking rebound from the demanded exit to the speakers' own exclusion. The live alternative is that f-s-q functions only as a moral label and carries no spatial echo here.

changed_reading.before: The speakers require the other group's exit so that their own group can enter.
changed_reading.after: The exit logic rebounds: their own group is separated, marked by an exit image, and held outside while the land becomes inaccessible to them.

surprising_valid_outliers.containment: This is surprising because it uses the packet's secondary q-l-l mapping for قالوا rather than the dominant speech root. It remains anchored to the exact focus word and is contextually activated by fear becoming visible; downstream prose should present it only as experimental split-root wordplay, not as the lexical derivation of قالوا.
surprising_valid_outliers.focus_anchor: قالوا at 5:22 through its packet-provided secondary mapping, together with the clause's repeated but deferred body-movements.

activation_trace.role: A bodily tremor from fear lets the opening utterance register unsettledness somatically rather than merely state a plan.
Instability and displacement make the elaborate verbal movement an analogue for bodies that do not cross the boundary.
Fear becoming visible supplies the contextual trigger for hearing instability in the focus utterance.
Deferred bodily entry contrasts with the immediate motion performed inside the speakers' language.

changed_reading.before: The opening speech calmly states a tactical condition.
changed_reading.after: The speech can be carried as a verbal tremor: conditional language moves repeatedly while the speakers' bodies remain unstable before the threshold.

surprising_valid_outliers.containment: This is surprising because it activates repair, splinting, and interlocked-part branches rather than the ordinary coercive sense of جبارين. It remains anchored in جبارين, the repeated entry/exit construction, and the adjacent gate; downstream prose should qualify it as a material-spatial analogy, never as a translation of the residents' title.
surprising_valid_outliers.focus_anchor: جبارين joined to the repeated inside/outside movement of the focus ayah.

activation_trace.role: Repairing a fracture lets the residents be imagined as what holds the occupied territory together.
A splint that binds a break gives the occupants a structural, binding role in the speakers' mental map.
Interlocking parts convert the repeated entry language into an image of a closed, body-like interior.
The concrete entrance counters the imagined total closure by identifying one penetrable threshold.

changed_reading.before: The occupants are simply overpowering fighters.
changed_reading.after: The speakers may imagine them as the binding structure of the occupied space itself, so removal seems necessary before entry even though the counter-voice points to a gate.

strongest_changes: The focus condition reverses the prescribed forward trajectory by assigning the first movement to the occupants.
The gate sequence exposes a causal inversion: the speakers demand the practical result of victory before crossing the threshold.
The next speech hardens a formally open condition into indefinite sitting and outsourced action.
The demanded exit rebounds onto the refusing group through separation, prohibition, and wandering outside.
summary.what_was_special: Repeated enter/exit verbs became a causal and spatial diagram rather than a generic refusal. The packet's f-s-q image and secondary q-l-l mapping also preserved two contained readings that a conservative synthesis would likely erase.
remaining_uncertainties: The object and construal of fear in 5:23 remain open, so the affective contrast cannot be made exclusive.
The covenant frame may expose a counter-covenant, or the speakers may understand themselves as claiming a tactical exception.
The f-s-q exit rebound, q-l-l tremor, and splinted-territory analogy may be reader-activated wordplay rather than active rhetoric.
